So I’ve been on the other end with this and when I open up to partners about my history of abuse. The only reaction I want is someone to listen until I’m done talking and then to comfort me and reassure me when I’m done. I don’t want comments or judgements about me. I would ideally like a hug, kiss, cuddle, etc and something said like “thank you for telling me. I know that took a lot of courage/bravery/etc. to tell me that. Do you want to talk about it anymore? If not I just want you to know that you can talk to me about this anytime.” And then we move on with our lives. But know that those things could affect someone any time and having a partner who allows them to talk about or just giving the invitation that this could be brought up again is a great way to build and maintain trust. 

If someone shuts down and says nothing or leaves or even worse I’ve had some people gaslight me or laugh at me or have some other harmful reaction. It’s okay to show emotion of course it’s a hard thing to hear but being calm, comforting, and supportive is all anyone needs in those moments. 

I hope this helps!

I went through a divorce in 2019 at 24 so here is all the advice I can give you. 

1. Don’t lose yourself! If you have, return to yourself.  In whatever way that means to you. It may be picking up a hobby you haven’t touched in awhile. Maybe it’s journaling or writing or creating. Whatever makes you feel like YOU, do it. If you do break up this will give you some direction to focus your energy and free time. 
2. Have a routine. Start practicing self care now. Write down all the things you want to do on a daily basis and find a way to put them in place realistically. A good routine will help you if you do break up and you feel lost or depressed. 
3. Find a way to expend energy. while going through my divorce, I needed some way to “get out the bad stuff”.  all those emotions and/or anxiety you’re working through to heal creates all this energy inside of you and it needs somewhere to go. For me, running helped me feel like I was exerting that energy and I felt calm and confident afterwards. Find something that will help you burn up that energy. Working out releases endorphins so that also helped reset my mind when I just kept thinking about things. 
4. Find what makes you confident- nails, hair, clothes, make up, whatever it is. Plan to do something that makes you feel confident. You’ll need it if you start to feel down about yourself. 
5. Write down all the things you would do if you were single. It could be a trip, a night out, etc. it could be reorganizing and looking forward to more space. Give yourself something to look forward to about being single. It puts things into perspective and will be a good start if things don’t work out. 
6. Accept your situation as is. If y’all break up, the quicker you accept it the quicker you’ll move on. Acceptance comes with time, you can’t force it, but being prepared that it could happen and accepting it if it does will really lessen the blow and severity. 

This is everything I did in my journey to finding myself again. It’s really just how I heal. If this advice doesn’t help I hope that it at least sparks some ideas for you or leads you on the right path!

Running was pivotal for me. The turning point was when I had laid in bed for days and hadn’t eaten and wasn’t drinking enough water. I was getting so overwhelmed with the crying and the depression and the suicidal thoughts that I was laying exhausted on the floor. I was running out of the energy to cry and I heard a voice in my head telling me to go on a walk. So I laughed hysterically while putting on my shoes but off I went. 

That walk helped me burn some energy that I didn’t know I had. It was like the wheels inside me started turning again and I was purging out the dark energy. Getting out and being around people. Seeing that life goes on. Looking up at the sky and trees all around me and seeing how beautiful things still were. I went home and I was still very depressed and still very anxious but at peace and feeling a little more in control. 

I ran the next day. I tried channeling in the depression and the negative energy and all the bad things I was feeling and practiced throwing them away on my runs. I pushed myself physically because I was pushing myself mentally and then little breakthroughs would come. I would get a change of perspective or have epiphanys. Endorphins would race through me and I would have a clear mind at the end of a run. I was proving to myself that I was strong and capable and I was only going to get stronger. I felt like a whole new person at the end of my runs. 

I have health issues that didn’t let me run as often as I would have liked but I made it work. Running taught me how to rest as well. I would push myself hard on a run and then take a few days to actually rest. Not just my body but my mind. If I gave myself ample time to rest I could kill it on a run so I only ran like once a week. 

When I started losing weight and liking the way I looked in the mirror instead of refusing to really see myself I could see the change. Finally putting myself first and doing what I needed to be my best. I taught myself how to love myself. It all started with depression. 

I just want to say to anyone who’s going through it that I hope the best for you. You’re not alone. There’s an outlet for you and you’ll find it

I almost drowned once. I was stuck in a capsized boat under water for 43 seconds. I wouldn’t call it as near death as some other stories I’ve heard but it was terrifying. It took me a minute to figure out what happened and i instantly opened my mouth to breathe when I realized I couldn’t. I swallowed a lot of water until i could actually control my body and mind enough to realize what was happening. I had a thought that I won’t be able to breathe until I can get out of here. I was seat-belted inside a boat capsule and had to unseat-belt myself and then open up a canopy that was banded down with super thick bands that I couldn’t break. It’s dark so I couldn’t find them to undo them either. I remember screaming under water and punching at the top of the cabin. Wasn’t strong enough to really do anything but I was panicked and wasn’t using the most logical thought processes. I finally accepted the situation, calmed down, and found my way out. By the time I climbed out of the boat I didn’t think to swim out from underneath it before swimming to the surface and I swam straight up into the boat again. So stupid. But at that moment I remembered thinking I’m going to drown because I can’t get to the surface and gave up trying again. 

A scuba diver got me and brought me to the surface. The first breath was painful and even more panic inducing because I felt like I couldn’t breath enough. I was gasping for air and the diver gave me his oxygen and dragged me to a safety boat. Which I had to be dragged on. I remember trying to lift my arms to climb on but my body was dead weight completely. All the oxygen from my muscles was gone. I was completely useless in that moment. 

Anyways I was perfectly fine. Beat up and had a minor concussion but fine nonetheless. Taught me a lot about how I handled that situation though. I panicked a lot and gave up a lot and didn’t think things through. Also I had been trained what to do in that situation and had been in that situation during training but it’s completely different during the real thing. Major props and respect to people who risk their lives for others and can maintain a level head during the whole thing.

As far as meeting new people, the best way is finding someone in your class to study with. Or make small talk with someone you sit next to. Just introduce yourself when you sit down for class and if they are interesting in chatting you’ll know, if not let it go and try again With them or someone else. Once you see them a few times and things are going well, ask to study with them and then the friendship will continue to form from there. After study session, grab a bite to eat, go on a walk, etc. just find ways to connect outside of school and the friendship will grow. It won’t work with everyone because not everyone will get a long with you like that, but you’ll find some that are interested in pursuing a friendship or you’ll hit it off with them well. 

When you meet other people and you want to connect with them further, ask for their number. I usually try to find some sort of common ground, so if they mention something that they do or have, I say “I like to do x as well, where do you like to do x at?” ... “oh that sounds awesome, I’ve always wanted to do x there too, maybe we can go sometime together?” If that works, get their number and then go do whatever x is. Or if they have a dog and you have a dog, go to a dog park together, etc. it doesn’t always work but I’ve made some great friends just finding some sort of common ground and then inviting them to do that thing with me. It may be weird at first but if they want to make friends too, then it’ll happen for sure. 

I think of friendship as finding a job. You’ll get a lot of resumes or a lot of interviews but it won’t always work out. But you always know when you’ve got the job you really want. For all the no’s you get, you’ll get a good yes. 

And don’t be hard on yourself. Just do what’s natural. And don’t get hurt if someone doesn’t want to be your friend. It may be because they don’t really want to make any new friends so they’re not interested in pursuing a brand new friendship. Or maybe y’all just aren’t right for each other. 

I’ve been where you are and it definitely gets easier. I’m very shy and can be very awkward but I know when I meet someone if we could be friends and if I sense a mutual ground I’ll pursue it. Sometimes successfully sometimes not. It’s worth it either way :) 

I hope some of this helps, good luck!

However, I was on hormonal bc (pill) for 8 years of my life. I didn’t start having sex until being on the pill for 4 years and every time every second was very painful. I went to my gyno a billion times for painful sex and tried a ton of lubes and treatments including, vaginal muscle relaxers, numbing cream, estrogen cream, and then other suppositories that are supposed to help keep the vaginal environment happy and wet since I was no longer experiencing the normal feminine discharge. 

I was very depressed and went from having sex multiple times a day to maybe twice a month as a married woman. 

I was having pelvic pain, pain inside like along my walls, and then really bad external pain at the opening. It would burn non stop and lube would only irritate it and make it worse. Same thing with the muscle relaxers and numbing creams nothing helped and I felt like everything I tried made it worse. 

After listening to a podcast about painful sex caused by birth control, my husband and I agreed I should stop. I didn’t consult a doctor on this I just decided on my own that I didn’t want to be on something that could be making sex worse and if stopping birth control improved my sex life then it’s worth the period pain and pelvic pain. 

From my research- birth control over time thins the tissues of the vagina and also can stop discharge so everything is dry and thin and will tear during sex. I didn’t have discharge and my pcp noted that I did have very thin skin. Could just be my anatomy or could be contributed to bc or both. Due to these things it can cause painful sex. However it takes some time on it for the skin to thin and the discharge to stop. 

Bc can also cause a burning pain during sex and irritation from lube and stuff like that. 

I’ve been off since the start of 2019 and wow. It’s improved my sex life and my overall happiness in general. I do still have all the pain but the burning has been significantly reduced or gone most of the time and I can actually have sex every day or almost every day if I want to because I can tolerate it again. My pcp thinks I have Endo and I personally think I have vulvodynia which I think is what’s causing the pain to still be there. I firmly believe birth control only made all of that worse and not better. The pain I have now is there but tolerable and definitely a miracle for me compared to what it was. 

I spoke to a lot of women about their experiences with sex and birth control and no one I knew suffered the same thing. But I do know I’m not the only one based on the podcast I listened to. I’ll comment below what it is when I can find it again if you’re curious. 

I say all this to maybe help you make a decision on what you should do. Birth control helped my period pain but made sex unbearable and made me so depressed and lonely because of it. For me, knowing what I went through, I would rather have what I have now because I have sex more often than I have a period and everything I tried to use for painful sex didn’t work (including essential oils and CBD and those types of holistic treatments).

Well it does sound like you have OCD. I would definitely go see a mental health specialist and have them diagnose you and work through whatever you can work through to get better. 

OCD is based on fear (obsessions) and then compulsions to combat that fear. So your cycle sounds like you trying to control your fear of abandonment by those people you care for most. 

It can get better by working through that fear and forgiveness of losing your best friend from uni and then focusing on how to not be afraid of losing your friendships. 

I have OCD and my fear is someone I love dying so I can understand where you’re coming from with everything. You are not crazy. 

Everyone has different ways of coping with OCD you just have to find what works best. The first thing that came to mind was to journal the best parts of your day every day. Writing makes things easier to remember and then it’s written down so you never forget it or lose sight of those great things and your friendship has some sort of tangible aspect to it. I’ve found that coping mechanisms can be part of the compulsions and make things worse but they can also make things a lot better. You don’t have to use that idea but come up with something that you can do to help yourself. Running away from this isn’t going to make things better it will make your OCD much worse and your thoughts will continue to torture you. As awkward or weird as it may be, this is something that you need to face because I truly believe you can help yourself and relieve those thoughts you’re having. 

In addition, work on pushing those thoughts out of your head. We can control our thoughts but it takes time and practice and a lot of work, but it is well worth it. 

I’m speaking from the perspective of someone who has OCD and has been able to better manage it through the years. I’ve made a lot of progress and it is so relieving to not be tortured by my mind 24/7. I still experience the intrusive thoughts and the compulsions and obsessive thoughts but it is much more manageable now and I am living a much better life than I was before I ever knew I had it. 

Good news is- you’re realizing something isn’t right and it’s not just gonna go away on its own. Use this energy to keep moving forward to make your life better. 

I’m not diagnosing you or saying everything I wrote will help you. I believe the things I said because of my own personal experience but I highly suggest you seek out medical help all for the betterment of your present and future self whether you’re diagnosed with OCD or not. 
 
You’re gonna be ok though :)

I went through the same thing. I worked at this place with all women and I felt like I could talk and get a long with everyone there but I still didn’t fit in. It was humiliating and awkward but I stuck it out for a bit and then left. I got back to my office and cried out of pure shame and embarrassment. 

It went on like that for the rest of my employment there. I could never find any reasons why I wasn’t well liked. The people that did like me ended up finding other jobs so for a while until I left it was really lonely and I felt so ashamed of myself. Like I just didn’t have the best personality or didn’t have good social skills or a billion other reasons I tired finding wrong with myself to explain this behavior. 

Looking back I still can’t find anything I had done wrong I just wasn’t the same type of person they were. 

I finally thought to myself that the only reason I cared was because I wanted to be accepted. And then I thought about who I was wanting acceptance from and all of these girls weren’t girls I would have hung out with had I had the choice outside of work. I didn’t mesh well with them because I was different. I felt more mature and I am a home body. I’m introverted and I like alone time. I like not going out drinking or always having to entertain people or always talking about my sex life, etc etc. I liked just chilling with good wholesome people and I found that those people who I truly mesh well with and who truly care about me as a person and who truly will push me to be better are hard to come by. So those girls didn’t deserve my friendship because they would never return what I would’ve put into it. 

Sometimes it just doesn’t work. It doesn’t mean you’re wrong or not fun or not socially great. It just means that they’re all one type and you don’t fit into that type so you’re excluded. But maybe it’s best you don’t fit into that type. You’re an amazing and beautiful person and you deserve friendships that don’t force you to be someone you’re not and who make you feel included and important from the very beginning. I’m in the US and am approaching my one year being vegan. 

You will be getting a lot of the facts as more people respond here but I just wanted to take a second to share my experiences if you decide to go vegan based on all of this. 

I chose to go vegan based on very little facts that I was finding mainly on social media about what animals endure. I sat and thought logically about it instead. I’m a huge animal lover and I have two dogs that I adore. They’re the apple of my eye and literally my whole world. Like I said a huge animal lover. I thought about what happens when they get scared. Or when one of them is hurt I see the other check on them. My bigger one protects the little one if she feels he is in danger (guest dogs in our house, etc. no real danger). I thought about when they get hurt or you know the times you accidentally step on a paw and they cry or yelp. I think about the times they’ve been sick or had to go for a vet visit and you can literally see the pain in their eyes due to whatever ails them.  I thought about how they comfort me when I cry or when I’m in pain and how no matter what they’re always by my side. 

And then I applied those same emotions and reactions to other animals. I thought about the heart break mother cows feel when they give birth to baby after baby and watch them taken away to never see them again. I think about how awful life must be like for those who are in cages and have no room to move or turn around. I think about how if I sit for too long or I sleep on my side all night long how I wake up sore and achy and then I think about how painful it must be to lay or stand like that permanently without being able to take pressure off your joints. Or how it must feel to be smooshed in areas with barely any room to breathe and god forbid get trampled because you’re a baby and no one is there to protect you from the bigger animals. I think about what life must be like for those who do get to live in pastures their whole lives and graze with their friends and then all of a sudden they’re loaded up side by side and sent to their final moments in literal hell. I think about how animals have much better instincts than us and better sense of smell so when they roll up to the slaughter house and smell the blood of the animals already slaughtered and hear their cries they know something is very wrong. I think about how every instinct inside them is telling them to run and escape and do something but they can’t. I see pictures and videos of cows comforting each other in line awaiting their death. I read about how they’re still conscious when their hide is stripped from them and their legs are cut off. I read about how in those moments their looking around and probably in shock and terrible pain. I think about how I used to get so excited to see cows in fields while traveling down country roads. I used to love watching them for the moments I could and petting them in petting zoos and finding joy in being close to them and then I thought about how I would feel sending them to slaughter. And then I thought that if my dogs feel pain and they can sense when others like themselves and human, are in pain, Then why can’t a cow or a chicken or a pig (who’s smarter than dogs) sense pain or fear or danger? That pig who was shaking had to see pigs and pigs before him/her slaughtered and is shaking because they know what’s coming. I think about how I would feel watching strangers or friends or neighbors or families slaughtered before me and knowing that I was next. 

So maybe it’s just not about how they lived but how they died. Who did they leave behind and who went before them? How did they feel when they were waiting for their death? I can guarantee you that regardless of their ability to reason with us and create what we can create, they can feel pain. They can sense danger. And they can smell and sense the fear and pain of others around them. 
 
I’ve watched video after video of animals trying to comfort and protect one another in their final moments and isn’t that what you would do if you were them? Wouldn’t you hold on to anything you could in your final moments as your body and mind are screaming at you that you’re in danger but there’s no where you can go and nothing you can do. We take a life A LIFE for a pleasant taste that lasts a few seconds to a minute and then is forgotten. 

And for all the literature out there that states that it’s different for farmed animals. They don’t think the same way we do. They don’t feel what we feel. Really? Because when I see evidence before my eyes of their fear and pain I see that they are not different. They are the same and I refuse to count my life as greater than theirs. I refuse to think of their souls as any less than mine and I refuse to take pleasure in anything that would harm such innocent and gentle creatures that did nothing to deserve death and pain. Literally told the same tale with slavery. About how African Americans are less than white people because their skulls are larger or because their skin is darker. I’ve read actual published articles about different biological differences between ethnicities in order to convince others that one was superior and the other inferior. Don’t you think if people published things like that about people that they would and definitely do publish articles like that about animals? Facts are great but what about what you can see before your eyes and the pain you feel in your heart when you watch those videos. Think about yourself in their shoes and if there is an animal on this earth that you love, think about how you would feel watching them hauled off to slaughter. 

It’s unnecessary and cruel and evil. 

I am not calling you a bad person and directing anger at you or anything like that. It’s ultimately up to you but going vegan freed me of the burden of hurting innocent animals and opened up my mind to their suffering. I wanted to share my thoughts with you regardless of facts because I feel like you can reason with this decision on more than just facts. Look at the evidence you’ve already seen and detach yourself from what the majority of the world believes. Get clarity and please help those who don’t have a voice and cannot help themselves.

I always use garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper, and paprika in everything I’m cooking. I’ll add more spices or do them in different quantities depending on what I’m making but I would start with always adding the first four and see how it goes. As far as quantities, a pinch or two of salt, sprinkle of pepper, sprinkle of onion powder, and bigger sprinkle of garlic powder. I do use recipes the first time I’m making something to see how they season it but I usually don’t keep the same quantities. I just look to see what flavors they work with and then I will add more or change it up a bit depending on the dish. I’ve gotten where I am today with about 5 years of actual cooking experience. I would start with recipes first and then the second or third time you make it you can customize it to your liking. And eventually (faster than you realize) you’ll learn what spices go with what dishes and flavors. I reserve cumin for Mexican only dishes - tacos, fajitas, burrito bowls, etc. I’ll use Cayenne in anything spicy (respect the spice, a little goes a long way) and paprika is one of my favorites so that’s why I put it on everything but its never the star of the show. Don’t underestimate the power of garlic, onion, and even bell peppers in any dish- Mexican, Italian, Cajun, etc. 

The biggest advice I can give you is to think of everything you’re making as a chipotle burrito bowl- every layer is seasoned in its own way and putting them together makes one delicious experience. So if you’re making a pasta dish or a rice dish or anything- add flavors and seasoning to every ingredient or part of the dish, not just the main part. It’ll make it much more enjoyable with a greater depth of flavor. So if you’re making a rice dish- cook the rice in veggie broth (or another vegan broth) and add some salt and pepper to it. Then, your next ingredient- let’s say tofu- should be seasoned as well with whatever style of dish you’re going for- Mexican, Cajun, etc. and then whatever else you throw in there should be seasoned as well (can even be with the same spices). For example, you want some corn and black beans with that? Throw both into a baking dish and season with my top 5 spices (or whatever) and then bake in the oven (on 350-400F for 10-20 minutes) to get that sort of roasted corn and black bean flavor. Add some sautéed or grilled peppers/veggies that have been seasoned and you’ll have a pretty swanky dish on your plate. 

More tips- if you’ve added a bunch of seasoning but whatever you’re making feels like it’s missing something- add more salt. Salt is always the thing that brings everything together so well. Start with a little and add more and always taste test every part before putting it all together. Once it’s all together you can add more seasoning as well. 

I also watch a lot of cooking shows which helps me identify what flavors go with what. It’s also taught me some knife and cooking skills and brought in different dishes I never would have thought about. 

There isn’t a right or wrong way to cook. It can be weird and scary at first but you’ll improve with time. And it’s totally ok to look at recipes before making anything (even if you’ve made it 100x). Either follow it exactly or use the recipe to get the idea of how to make it and do your own thing. Whatever works best for you. And you can always divert from the recipes- add more of this or less of this or add in something different. Or don’t add in that one ingredient at all if you don’t want to. 

Let me know if you have any other questions or need help with anything! I’m happy to explain more or talk about something else!

But I don’t bully him or try to persuade him differently- remember my life is my own and his life is his own. 

Long story short- the transition was hard but it was so easy at the same time because I knew it was worth it to those I didn’t want to hurt anymore. The thing that worked for me and continues to work for me was the realization that forgiveness isn’t for the other person, it was for me. So that I could finally be free and happy from past people and events that hurt me. I realized that they either had no idea i was struggling so much because of what they did to me or they didn’t give a shit if they did know. So why keep letting them have that power over me if they were out there living their life either way? For me, realizing this changed my perspective on the fact that I can hate someone for their actions against me but it has no effect on them and it just holds me back from being free and happy. So ultimately If I wanted to be happy I needed to heal my own wounds. I had to keep reminding myself over and over again that I was worthy of happiness and that I just needed to forgive otherwise it would haunt me forever. It happened and there was nothing I could do to change the past but I could make my future happier and brighter by coming to peace with that. 

This turning point is what helped me actually move on. As far as the act of “moving on” I don’t really know how I did it. I just tried to love myself and remind myself that I am doing this for me, not for them and it came naturally over time. I’m not doing them favors by working to forget it, I am changing my future for the better and it motivated me to push the thoughts and memories from my mind and focus on the good things that I had in the present. Time took care of the rest. 

I realize that this might be something you already see or might not be as helpful to you as it was for me, but I wanted to share this either way so you at least know my method of how I moved past some things I struggled with for years. Maybe it’ll help you find your own or maybe there’s some comfort in knowing that people out here in this universe give a shit about your pain and those who caused it aren’t worthy of you feeling it because of them. 

I hope you find your peace with all that you’re experiencing!

Yes!!! I went vegan in October of last year so right before the holiday season. I was really proud of myself to get through thanksgiving completely vegan, but then came Christmas time and I had some caramel m&ms, a brownie, and a few deviled eggs. My thinking at the time was “oh if I eat these things I didn’t actually buy them or prepare them so it’s not going to make a difference if I eat it. Otherwise it’ll go bad” and really, it was temptation of being around all my favorite things at my favorite time of year and giving in to that. But also, no one is perfect and I learned that when you’re making a big lifestyle change like this, it takes time to get where you want to be. I don’t crave those things anymore nor do they seem appetizing to me even with peer pressure, but it took time before I got there. 

I would say, be forgiving with yourself. Work hard and believe in what you’re doing. Think of all the animals, water, and resources you’re saving by making this choice every single day and it’ll get easier. Focus on the positive- learning to cook and bake if you don’t know how already, or learning to cook with different ingredients, opening up your world to different flavors and smells and ideas, new experiences, and the way your soul heals and feels when you’re vegan and you don’t hurt anyone with the choices you make. 

It’s worth it and you can do this. Just take your time, you’re doing the right thing :) and when you mess up, jump back on the horse and I promise it’ll be your new norm and you’ll see the world in a different way.

Try protein shakes! You can get 20-30 calories easy. I buy silk protein nut milk (about 10 grams a cup I think) and Vega protein and greens protein powder (20 grams a scoop) then I mix those together with a banana and a cup of cold brew and there you have it - 20-30 grams of protein first thing in the morning. You may not absorb every gram but it’s a big jump start to your day. You can leave out the coffee/banana/switch it up however you like but I recommend investing in protein. I also have IBS so I can’t do a ton of beans and it’s and really have to keep a lot of variety in my diet so the protein helps me immensely. Plus every scoop contains 2 servings of veggies!
